batches.risk: RM-49 is a BEHAVIOUR change on repositories that are healthy today, and both halves are deliberate: a folder whose frontmatter `name` disagrees with its directory is now reported and SKIPPED by `ls`, `ls member` and `ls project` — `skillRecords`, the README reader and `findSkill` all already refuse it, so `ls` was advertising skills `install` would not resolve — and a skipped people file no longer hides the roster, though its member's install counts become ABSENT rather than zero and must be reported as such. verification.corrections:
VERDICT: the batch's substance survives — every owner file, field, verb and precedent it relies on exists exactly as claimed, and nothing in the delta closed, renamed or moved any of it. Seven corrections, two of them material.

WHAT I VERIFIED CLEAN (no correction needed)
- All four cliChanges anchors are byte-correct at both revs: LsArgs src/commands/ls.ts:17, LsSkill :18, LocalSection :19, LsResult :20; RM-49's fail-whole enumeration is the readdir at ls.ts:50 and `if (!parsed.ok) throw new Error(\`Invalid skills/${name}/SKILL.md: ...\`)` at ls.ts:54 (not :53-56, as the correction says); the per-row degradation precedent is the latestTree `.catch` at ls.ts:59, which prints one line and returns '—'. The `ls` twin's model, search.test.ts:155 ("skips and reports a malformed skill folder while returning healthy matches"), exists.
- appHalf correction (3) is right on both halves: ls.ts:44 is `io.print(\`Local skills: ${invocation(args.form, 'ls --local')}\`)` and the staleness sentence is ls.ts:150.
- STALENESS: src/commands/ls.ts, src/commands/search.ts, src/lib/readme.ts and src/lib/skills.ts are blob-IDENTICAL at b5c0507, 85cc276 and f8557c4; `git log b5c0507..HEAD -- ls.ts search.ts readme.ts` is empty at both checkouts. No commit in the delta closes, renames or moves any row in this batch. (Note the delta is 27 commits b5c0507..85cc276, not 24.)
- SIMPLE bar intact: no owner-file field (LsSkill/SearchHit/LsResult are in-process TypeScript interfaces), no new verb, no new flag, no guard change, no team.json row. Approver is Ryan for all five rows (costing:72, :73, :82, :84, :121) — one approver, condition (6) holds.

CORRECTION 1 — dependsOn ["S7a"] MUST BE CUT (batch is not blocked by anything). S7a is MOOT: package.json at f8557c4 still declares only type/bin/files, no main, no exports, no types (cli-main/package.json:14-22), and the shipped delivery path is frame mode. S7f needs no prerequisite at all: the adapter validates the search payload with a `.passthrough()` zod schema declared "as of terum-skills 0.1.5" (desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:30), so `description`, `grants`, `installers` and `updated` are additive on the wire the day they land, and hello.protocol stays 1 (docs/frame-protocol.md:61-63).

CORRECTION 2 (MATERIAL) — the appHalf is written against a route that no longer exists, and must be re-pointed at the wire. The costing's own App-side for RM-38 says "The app runs `git -C <clone> log -1 --format=%cI -- skills/<name>` itself, once per skill" (costing:962); RM-02/RM-03/RM-49's app halves lean the same way on reading the clone. That is impossible in the shipped shell. The Rust side exposes exactly five commands — cli_spawn (lib.rs:39), cli_write (:93), cli_kill (:102), read_app_state (:114), host_platform (:126) — and cli_spawn runs only `Command::new(&node).arg(&entry).arg("--frames").args(&args)` (lib.rs:42-43). There is no shell plugin, no `git`, no filesystem read beyond ~/.terum/skills/run/app.json. So for all five rows the CLI payload is now the ONLY route, which strengthens the batch but changes its appHalf: every field must arrive as a verb `result.value`, and the app half is (a) deleting the fabricated description at desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:70 (`description: \`${hit.category} · by ${hit.author} · ${hit.installs} installs...\``) once RM-30 lands, and (b) widening cliSearch (index.ts:30) — plus a real `library()`/`skill()` mapping, which today returns the hard-coded gap (index.ts:64, :65). Target desktop/src/backend/tauri as well as mock/.

CORRECTION 3 (MATERIAL) — the batch contradicts itself on the printed line. The tests line says "`LsSkill` carries the SKILL.md description verbatim and the printed line is unchanged" (RM-30's wording, costing:911) while RM-38 — in this same batch — adds `updated` to `format()` at src/commands/ls.ts:84: "the §6 `ls` line format gains exactly one segment for both" (costing:961), and RM-38's own field bullet says "format() at src/commands/ls.ts:84 gains one more '; ' segment". Restate as: the printed line gains EXACTLY ONE segment (`updated`) and no other; `description` is a payload field and is never printed; `search` inherits the change automatically because it prints through the same function (search.ts:60 calls `formatSkill`).

CORRECTION 4 — appHalf correction (2)'s tail is wrong on code reality. The predicate claim is right (ls.ts:68 is `skills.filter((skill) => normalizeAuthor(skill.author) === normalizeAuthor(\`${member.display_name} <${member.email}>\`))`, matching costing:1269), but ls.ts:71 is the **Authored:** print line, not "Installed:" — `io.print(\`  Authored: ${authored.map(...).join(', ') || '—'}\`)`. "Installed:" is ls.ts:72.

But `readReadmeData` calls the SAME `readPeople` at readme.ts:128, and that reader is the fail-closed one (it throws on a folder/frontmatter name mismatch at readme.ts:135). Tolerance must therefore be added AT THE `ls` CALL SITE, never inside `readPeople`. The precedent is again in-family and file-local: search.ts:37 already does per-file `readPerson(...).catch(...)` + print + `.filter(person => person !== undefined)` under the comment "one unreadable member file is reported and skipped, never fatal for the team". Cite that, not just ls.ts:59.

CORRECTION 7 — RM-49's skills half has a cheaper, already-written implementation the cliChanges does not name. `ls` hand-rolls its enumeration (readdir ls.ts:50 + parseSkillFrontmatter :53 + throw :54), whereas `skillRecords` (src/lib/skills.ts:20-39) already does BOTH halves of RM-49: it skips a bad folder through `options.onProblem` (:34-36) AND enforces the folder-name/frontmatter-name match the risk section describes — `if (parsed.data.name !== name) throw new Error(\`Skill folder ${name} does not match frontmatter name ${parsed.data.name}.\`)` (skills.ts:32) — which is also exactly why `findSkill` refuses such a folder (skills.ts:47-48). Routing `listSkills` through `skillRecords(clone, team, { onProblem: ... })` — the same call search.ts:35 makes — delivers RM-49's skills half and RM-30's `description` (SkillRecord carries `frontmatter`) in one edit, instead of duplicating the check inside ls.ts.

MINOR — "readme.test.ts" in the tests line is ambiguous: two files carry that name (src/commands/__tests__/readme.test.ts, for the `readme` verb, and src/lib/__tests__/readme.test.ts). `latestChange` (RM-38) and `installersById` (RM-03) are library functions in src/lib/readme.ts, so the costing names src/lib/__tests__/readme.test.ts. Say which.

NOT VERIFIABLE FROM THE MATERIAL SUPPLIED — appHalf correction (1)'s double-placement claim. CP-20 is confirmed SIMPLE · app, owner `none`, approver "none (Ryan, if RM-48's field is taken)" (costing:135, §8.1 SIMPLE·app list at :1878), and its content is precisely the disclosure rule inheriting ls.ts:150's sentence (costing:1236). Whether S7k's appHalf already carries it I cannot check — S7k was not provided. The deletion is safe either way (CP-20 needs no CLI change), but the "only double-placement in the plan" claim is unverified here.

SYNC RULE — verified correct. `installed[].since` is per-person and day-granular (src/lib/schema.ts:36-41) and `placements[].placed_at` is per-machine and never committed (schema.ts:100); neither answers "when did this skill last change". `updated` from committed history needs no propagation. verification.corrections:
S7f's five rows are real, read-only, and D20-clean, and every re-anchoring in `cliChanges` is correct — but the batch is not shippable as written. Six material corrections, three anchor fixes.

MATERIAL

1. `dependsOn: ["S7a"]` is a dead edge — CUT IT. S7a is MOOT per the delta: RM-11's exports map never shipped (`/tmp/.../cli-main/package.json:14-22` declares only `type`, `bin`, `files` — no `main`, `exports` or `types`) and the app reaches the CLI as a child process over frames, not as an import. S7f needs no library entry: its payload arrives as a verb's `result.value` on the wire (frames.ts:24 `ResultFrame{verb,ok,exitCode,error?,declined?,value?}`). Re-point to `dependsOn: []`. Nothing else in S7f depends on S7a's surviving half (CP-19 is a design-side printed-command gate that S7f does not touch).

2. The appHalf's RM-51 clause is UNIMPLEMENTABLE as costed and must move to `cliChanges`. Costing §3 (line 1269) specifies the author→person join as "written once in the Backend adapter … enumerate with skillRecords … read every people/<handle>.json". The shipped adapter cannot read files: `desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:137` registers exactly five commands — `cli_spawn, cli_write, cli_kill, read_app_state, host_platform` — and `read_app_state` reads only `~/.terum/skills/run/app.json` (lib.rs:113-122). There is no generic file read, and AGENTS.md invariant 1 forbids fs access outside `src/backend/` anyway. So the join must ship as a CLI-side payload on the `ls` result (per-skill author identity, or the buckets themselves), exactly as the delta forced on S7d's three "exported reader" rows. Correcting RM-51's line number while leaving it in the appHalf preserves a plan that cannot be built.

3. RM-38 has no seam DTO home, and "Recently updated" is not a sort. `SkillCard` (desktop/src/backend/types.ts:14) carries no last-changed field; neither does the fixture's `SKILLS` (src/fixtures/schema.ts:19) nor `CATALOG` (:21) — only `PROJECTS` has `updated` (:26). And the drawn control is a static default label, not a comparator: `SearchRow({…, sort='Recently updated', …})` in desktop/src/components/domain/Primitives.tsx:30, with no sort implementation anywhere in src/screens. So RM-38's app half is three things the batch does not scope — a new `SkillCard` field, a mock value for it on every fixture-derived card (AGENTS.md invariant 2: the mock renders every board as drawn), and an actual sort. Either state all three in the appHalf or split RM-38 into its own batch; the CLI half alone changes no pixel.

4. The `risk` paragraph describes a check `ls` does not have. `listSkills` reads each folder and refuses only on `!parsed.ok` (src/commands/ls.ts:54); it NEVER compares frontmatter `name` to the directory. The mismatch refusal lives in `skillRecords` (src/lib/skills.ts:32) and the README reader (src/lib/readme.ts:135). So RM-49 in `ls` ADDS a check that does not exist today — it does not merely change an existing failure mode. Rewrite the risk sentence accordingly; as phrased ("is now reported and SKIPPED") a Codex run would look for a check to soften and find none.

5. The "skipped people file" half of RM-49 is unspecified and touches the README path. `readPeople` (src/lib/readme.ts:142-144) is `Promise.all(files.map(… parseJson(personSchema, …)))` — one malformed file rejects the whole call, which ls.ts:33 turns into a whole-verb failure via the outer catch (ls.ts:46). `readPeople` has exactly two non-test callers: ls.ts:33 and src/lib/readme.ts:128. The fail-closed §9 guarantee the risk paragraph promises does NOT live in `readPeople` — it lives in `readReadmeData`'s tree readers (readme.ts:150-165, `Cannot generate README: … was removed from the tree`). So the batch must say whether it relaxes `readPeople` (and then prove readme.ts:128's caller stays fail-closed) or adds a degrading variant used only by `ls`. Also note the promised consequence — "install counts become ABSENT rather than zero" — has no representation in `LsSkill.installs: number` (ls.ts:18); absent needs `number | null` or a sibling field, which is an interface change the `cliChanges` section does not list.

6. The appHalf targets the retired standalone repo. The app is now `desktop/` inside the CLI monorepo; `/home/teniroo/Projects/terum-skills-app/src/backend/types.ts` is byte-identical to `desktop/src/backend/types.ts` (verified by diff), so the DTO reasoning survives, but the adapter does not: the standalone repo's `src/backend/tauri/` is still an empty README stub, while the real adapter is `desktop/src/backend/tauri/`. For RM-30 specifically the landing site is `desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:70`, which today FABRICATES the card description app-side — `description: \`${hit.category} · by ${hit.author} · ${hit.installs} installs${hit.unresolved ? ' · not in HEAD' : ''}\`` — over a loose `cliSearch` schema (index.ts:30) that reads no description field. Landing RM-30 in the CLI payload REQUIRES deleting that synthesis and extending `cliSearch` in the same PR, plus the mock. The appHalf names neither surface.

ANCHOR ERRORS

7. appHalf correction (2) is itself off by one: ls.ts:71 is `io.print(\`  Authored: …\`)`; the `Installed:` print line is ls.ts:72. The RM-51 predicate at :68 is correct as stated.

8. `readme.test.ts` is ambiguous — the repo has BOTH `src/commands/__tests__/readme.test.ts` and `src/lib/__tests__/readme.test.ts`. `installCounts` (src/lib/readme.ts:40) and `latestTree` (:119) are lib functions, so the target is `src/lib/__tests__/readme.test.ts`. Name it in full or a Codex run will edit the wrong file.

9. The malformed-folder twin in search starts at `search.test.ts:154` (`it('skips and reports a malformed skill folder while returning healthy matches', …)`); :155 is the fixture line inside it.

10. The single-owner argument for `src/commands/ls.ts` cites a batch that never touches it: "S7h owns the `--host` flag". Per the delta, S7h is TJ-04 (admin column) + TJ-05 (pending invitations), which live in invite.ts/team.ts and the gapped `roster()` — no ls.ts edit. Either the rationale means a different batch id or a third ls batch is missing from the plan. S7f/S7g's split (LsSkill/SearchHit/LsResult vs `LocalSection['rows']`) is correct and does hold.

The skew rule does belong to `stale` only: STAMP_SKEW_MS is hook.ts:151, read solely by stampIsFresh (hook.ts:166), which staleLine (hook.ts:171) consults. `status` is prompt-free (no io.confirm/text/select anywhere in status.ts), so the adapter's read() can drive it. `stampedAt` does not exist yet (grep of hook.ts) — correctly new work, and the hook.ts collision with S7l is real. C2 (must fix — this one silently defeats the batch) — the adapter DISCARDS `value` on a failing result, and `status` fails in exactly the states this batch exists to describe. desktop/src/backend/tauri/run.ts:71-73: `} else { const error = frame.error ?? 'terum-skills reported a failure.'; finish({ ok: false, error }, { t:'result', ok:false, error }); }` — no value is carried. Meanwhile status.ts:99-100 returns `failure(lines.join('\n'), { version, teams })` whenever ANY team is unreadable, and "unreadable clone" is precisely the absent/foreign/incomplete case for which the batch specifies `policy`/`categories` null while `pending`/`syncedAt` still report. The CLI side already does its half — execute.ts:32 passes `value: outcome.value` on the failing arm and frames.ts:174 writes `if (outcome.value !== undefined) frame.value = outcome.value` — so the loss is entirely in run.ts. The batch's own test ("reports a team's pending entries on the Result even when its clone is absent") would pass in vitest and still render the bare error string in the app. S7k must own one of: (a) an adapter change carrying `value` through the ok:false branch of run.ts, or (b) a CLI rule keeping `status` ok:true with per-team detail (which is a behaviour change RM-18/RM-31 also want). Neither is in cliChanges or appHalf today.

C3 (must fix) — the app half names only mock reading rules; the real adapter half is unwritten. Today `status: async () => gap('Team status in the design's shape (machine, me, teams, counts)')` at desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:61, with the gap string built at index.ts:32. The batch must add: a loose passthrough `cliStatus` zod schema beside cliSearch/cliValidate (index.ts:17-30, declared "as of terum-skills 0.1.5"), and `status: () => read(['status'], cliStatus, map)` using read() (index.ts:47-53). THE SEAM DROPS THE VALUE ON EXACTLY THE TEAMS THIS BATCH IS ABOUT. status returns `failure(lines.join('\n'), { version, teams })` whenever any team is unreadable (status.ts:99) — the absent-clone case the batch tests. batches.cliChanges: `src/cli.ts` — ONE new flag SHARED by both rows (which is the only reason TJ-05 is SIMPLE): `--host` on the `ls` chain (:93), refused with `--local`. `src/commands/ls.ts` — `LsArgs` (:17) gains `host?: boolean`; the roster entries gain `hostRole?: 'admin'|'member'|'unknown'` and `hostCheckedAt?: string`, and `LsResult` gains `invitations?: {login, invitedBy: string|null, invitedAt: string|null}[]` — in-process RETURN TYPES, never serialized, because admin is a host capability (§6.0) and the host is the only thing that enforces it, so the CLI reads it and forgets it. `--host` adds exactly two live GitHub reads: `repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators?permission=admin` for the roles, marking each roster handle whose `people/<handle>.json` `github` login appears in it Admin and every other active member with a non-empty `github` Member; and `repos/{owner}/{repo}/invitations` for the pending list — the same call `team remove` already makes to cancel them, with the `.filter(...)` that narrows to one login dropped (team.ts:115-117) — printing each invitee's login with the inviter and date only when GitHub supplies them and an em dash when it does not. A member whose `github` is `''` (schema.ts:60 permits it for a generic-git member) is `unknown`, NEVER Member: the CLI does not infer a role from a missing identity. Invitees are listed as INVITATIONS, never as members, and never counted in the roster, because `invite` writes nothing to the team repository (D9) so an invitee has no people file until they join. On a generic-git remote, without a logged-in `gh`, or on any refusal or failure — including a 403 to a non-admin caller, which GitHub and not the CLI decides — `--host` prints the §6.0 host message and the roster WITHOUT the column, `ls` still exits 0, and it never prints a remembered or inferred role. `ls` performs no `safeWrite` (ls.ts has no write path), so NO guard change; nothing about `ls` without `--host` changes.

Invited rows render blank Joined / Teams / Last-seen, exactly as drawn, because an invitee has no people file. The role chip gains a fourth state, `unknown`, for offline / no-gh / generic-git / empty github, and loses its chevron: `role_menu`'s two checkable role items have no verb (TJ-02 is design-side), while "Remove from team" does (`team remove`, team.ts:71). Delete GAPS.md:38's admin and pending-invitation clauses.

Correct these before it is buildable. 1. SEAM CONTRADICTION — "in-process RETURN TYPES, never serialized" is false under frame mode. The app cannot import a reader; the only channel is the result frame's `value` (frames.ts:24 `ResultFrame{verb,ok,exitCode,error?,declined?,value?}`; run.ts drops everything else). If `hostRole`/`hostCheckedAt`/`invitations` are "never serialized", the appHalf cannot exist. Reword to: these are never PERSISTED to any file (no config.json, no people file, no team.json — admin is host capability per §6.0); they ride `result.value` over frames and are additive against the adapter's passthrough zod schemas (index.ts:17-30, pinned "as of 0.1.5"). 2. dependsOn IS WRONG — it names the two batches that do not unblock it and omits the one that does. `roster()` is a hard-coded gap today (`roster: async () => gap('The roster')`, desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:69) and there is no CLI verb behind it. S7g is RM-39/RM-40/RM-44 on `ls --local` → `library()`; S7c is config.json label + identity flags. Neither produces the `Member` DTO (`Design['ROSTER'][number] & {status;projects;lastSeen;lastPublish}`, types.ts:25) that MemberRow renders. Without the batch that supplies role/projects/joined/lastSeen (S7b + the PF-05/PF-06 derivations), S7h's Status column has no row to attach to. Add S7b as a dependency (or the batch that maps a CLI verb onto `roster()`); keep S7g/S7c only as file-ordering deps and say so. 3. D20 IS MIS-ASSIGNED, AND S7h OWNS IT. The `role:` preference does NOT back S7b's job-title label — it overrides the Admin/Member CHIP. ShareScreen.tsx:45 `const saved=backend.prefs.get('role:'+m.handle,m.status), status=saved==='admin'||saved==='member'?saved:m.status;` and the menu at :48 writes `action.pref('role:'+m.handle,label.toLowerCase())`. The job title is a different field, rendered at :47 as `{m.handle} · {m.role}`. The SYNC ADDENDUM's line "role: (ShareScreen.tsx:45) with S7b" is therefore wrong: the per-PR D20 retirement of that key belongs to S7h, the batch that makes the chip host truth. The appHalf must state explicitly that it deletes the :45 read AND both :48 writes in the same PR. 4. TWO EXISTING DESKTOP TESTS BREAK AND ARE UNLISTED. desktop/src/screens/share/share.test.tsx:24 ('changes a per-handle role preference') asserts `backend.prefs.get('role:'+member.handle,'')` becomes 'admin' after clicking the Admin menuitem; :26 ('keeps role state intact when preferences cannot be written') asserts the Storage-full alert on `prefs.set`. Retiring the pref invalidates both. They must be rewritten in this PR. 5. THE `unknown` STATE DOES NOT RENDER — it silently prints "Member", which is precisely what the cliChanges forbids. ShareScreen.tsx:45 falls back to `m.status` for any value that is not 'admin'|'member', and :48 renders `{status==='admin'?'Admin':'Member'}` with class `'member-role '+status`. So an empty-`github` member marked `unknown` by the CLI displays as Member. The appHalf must name the render change at :48 (third label, e.g. "—"/"Unknown"), the new `.member-role.unknown` rule in share.css, and the aria label. 6. THE INVITED-ROW PAYLOAD DOES NOT SATISFY THE SEAM DTO. `Roster['invited']` is `Design['INVITED']` = `{handle,name,role,initials,invited,by}` (src/fixtures/schema.ts:28) and InvitedRow (ShareScreen.tsx:51) renders all six — ``, `{m.name}`, `{m.handle} · {m.role} · invited {m.invited} by {m.by}`. The proposed `{login, invitedBy, invitedAt}` supplies none of `name`, `initials`, `role`. GitHub's `repos/{o}/{r}/invitations` payload does carry `permissions` (which can serve `role`) and the invitee login, but `name` and `initials` have NO source — the batch itself argues an invitee has no people file. So either the CLI payload grows `permissions`, or `Roster['invited']` shrinks and the drawn row changes (a design-side call for Teddy, not an implementer's). Unstated either way. Note also that `invited`/`by` are display strings in the fixture while the CLI proposes ISO/login — the em-dash fallback is described only for the CLI's terminal print; the app needs its own. 7. THE ADMIN READ IS ALSO ALREADY WRITTEN, AND NEITHER READ HAS A DEADLINE. The rationale lifts only the invitations call, but `repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators?permission=admin` already exists at team.ts:108-111 with `--paginate --slurp`, `paginatedItems<{login?:string}>` and its own "Could not list repository admins" failure string — the shared reader should lift BOTH (:108-111 and :115-117) plus `paginatedItems`, or the duplication the batch is trying to avoid just moves. Separately: `RunOptions.deadlineMs` is optional (src/lib/runner.ts:5) and team.ts passes no options to either gh call, and the adapter's `read()` has no timeout of its own (index.ts:47-53) — so `ls --host` can hang the Share screen indefinitely. The risk line says "never make `ls` fail"; it must also say "never hang": pass an explicit `deadlineMs` and treat expiry as the §6.0 omit-the-column path. 8. GAPS.md — WRONG REFERENT AND A FORBIDDEN EDIT. desktop/GAPS.md:38 reads "Share / ShareInvite (role chip Admin · Member, invite scoping, last seen)"; there is NO pending-invitation clause on that line to delete. batches.title: install: per-item isolation and the Windows home derivation
batches.cliChanges: `src/commands/install.ts` — wrap the `install member` / `install project` loop bodies in try/catch, collect per-item errors, report the failing skill BY NAME, and continue, exactly as sync's endorsed batch already does (sync.ts:308-320); the Result carries every skill that DID place on `failure`'s third slot (src/lib/result.ts:1-6), and it is `ok:false` when any item failed, so the exit code still tells a script the batch was not clean while the successful `InstalledResult`s are reported as having happened — because those placements are already durable in `config.placements` and in the people file. TWO error classes are batch-FATAL and are rethrown rather than isolated: `PromptClosedError` (a channel that is gone is not a per-item failure — the same rule sync applies at sync.ts:181, :225, :317) and a remote-access or `safeWrite`-exhaustion failure, because `safeWrite` retries with backoff to a 30 s deadline before throwing, so isolating it would turn one unreachable remote into one retry-to-deadline loop per remaining item — eight of them behind the drawn "Install 8 skills" button. RM-21 replaces `placementHome`'s body (install.ts:241, today `store.root.endsWith('/.terum/skills') ? dirname(dirname(store.root)) : store.root`) with a `basename`/`dirname` walk that ascends only when the last two segments are literally `.terum` and `skills` — separator-correct on every platform, the same reason `join` is correct in the agent-paths table. The POSIX suffix test can NEVER match on Windows, where the default root is `C:\Users\<name>\.terum\skills`: it fell through, the store root itself became the home, and every global placement landed at `<store root>\.claude\skills`, a directory Claude Code never reads. Nothing is stored and nothing is derived from this process's HOME.
batches.appHalf: The two batch-install dialogs render per-item outcomes instead of one all-or-nothing error, naming the skills that landed and the skills that did not. ONE consequence the app must expect and disclose rather than treat as a leak: an isolated batch can leave one `config.pending` entry PER failed item where today a single throw leaves one — correct, because pending is written before placement and cleared only after the people-file write, sync replays pending (sync.ts:160-186), and a team with any pending entry is deliberately left unstamped (sync.ts:344-347) so the next session retries — but it changes what the next `sync --hook` does, and that is intended. The app's mid-operation surface reads those entries through S7k's `TeamStatus.pending`.
batches.rationale: A parallel lane owning `src/commands/install.ts` alone, placed before S7j because RM-18's install half needs this file's final shape. RM-21 rides it because it is the same file and because a Windows-broken global placement makes every app-side placement claim wrong on one of the two platforms M5 targets.
batches.risk: RM-19 changes what a partially-failed batch leaves behind, and therefore what the next session-start sync does. The tests must pin the pending-entry count, not just the placements.
batches.tests: `install.test.ts`: `install member` isolates one failing candidate — the others land, the failure names it, and the successes ride the failure Result; `PromptClosedError` and a RemoteAccessError abort the batch rather than isolating; one `config.pending` entry per failed item and the next `sync` replays each. `placementHome` resolves a `<home>/.terum/skills` root to `<home>` and leaves any other root alone, asserted on both basename predicates rather than on a separator literal (so the test itself is platform-neutral).

batches.cliChanges: New `src/commands/hook.ts` plus one registration in `src/cli.ts`'s M2 block. With no argument it prints the command actually FOUND in `~/.claude/settings.json` — read from the file, never from `HOOK_COMMAND` (src/lib/hook.ts:12, `npx -y terum-skills@latest sync --hook`) — or reports that no entry is installed, which is how a stale hook command becomes visible. `on` calls `installHook` (hook.ts:89) DIRECTLY rather than `offerHook` (:130): it does not short-circuit on an existing entry, so it is how a stale command is corrected on a machine that already has one, and it asks no y/N because a user who asks for the switch has given the consent. `off` calls `removeHook` (:116), which strips only this tool's commands and leaves a mixed group's other hooks intact, and it joins `team leave` of your last configured team and machine `uninstall` in the removal list. batches.title: The receipt reader and the §12 UI contract (IB-02 keeps its eval half here; its ls input is BM-04 in S7f)
batches.cliChanges: New `src/lib/evals/receipts.ts` exporting `latestReceipt(clone, skillId, version)` and the committed run list per version — the fourth reader of the rule `latestReceiptVerdict` already implements privately at src/lib/readme.ts:172-181 (readdir the version directory, take the lexicographically newest `.json`, validate it, ENOENT means absent), factored out so the README column, CI and the UI cannot drift. Plus one new read-only verb, `receipt <ref> [--skill-version <tree>] [--runs]`, registered as a SIBLING of `eval`, never as `eval show`, because `eval <skill>` already binds its positional (cli.ts:116) so a subcommand would be swallowed as the skill name. It reads the local team clone ONLY — never fetches, never writes, never recomputes — and a receipt whose `skill_id` or `version` disagrees with its PATH is treated as absent, exactly as the README column already does. It is deliberately FAIL-OPEN like that column and not fail-closed like the publish receipt check, so a malformed newest receipt makes the UI show no receipt while CI still blocks the publish; where the UI and CI can therefore disagree, CI is authoritative. Read-only means no `safeWrite`, no `GuardAction` and no `PEOPLE_ACTIONS` entry. CP-11, CP-15 and IB-02 carry NO code — they are three eval-engine §12 paragraphs: (a) a viewer-SET filter over a receipt field is permitted and is not a derived statistic, subject to two §5.4 constraints — a lift threshold applies only within one `(provenance.model, provenance.cc_version)` pair, so a surface either scopes itself to one pair or shows provenance beside the facet and EXCLUDES receipts from another pair rather than silently comparing them; and a filtered list is still ordered by install count (D38), never by the facet's own number; (b) every receipt-DERIVED facet ships OFF, the filter control shows a zero badge on first run, and the unfiltered catalog is what a new viewer sees, because a default PASS-only or lift-floor filter is the product ranking on the viewer's behalf using precisely the numbers our own probe shows do not rank (Spearman ρ −0.07 against SkillsBench all-harness, −0.22 against its claude-code column); (c) IB-02's cross-version paragraph ONLY if Teddy keeps `report_regression`'s figure, and then each receipt's own provenance line must sit beside its own numbers with the comparison SUPPRESSED entirely when model or cc_version differ.
batches.appHalf: The evals rail and report read through the seam's `receipts({skillId, version})` instead of the fixture, and the Marketplace filter control ships with a zero badge and no active facets on first run. The app must not promote a partial receipt (readme.ts:196-199's rule) and must not merge two receipts of one version into one figure, table or derived number. Delete GAPS.md:40.
batches.rationale: Serialization edge: both batches edit `src/cli.ts`'s eval region and the `src/lib/evals/` area. Placed second because the reader is the piece the app's whole evals surface hangs on, and it is cleaner to add it once the payload rows (EV-07, EV-08) have settled the types it returns.
batches.risk: The verb must be a sibling, not `eval show` — a subcommand under `eval <skill>` is silently swallowed as the skill name, which is a bug commander will not report.
batches.tests: `src/lib/evals/__tests__/receipts.test.ts`: returns the lexicographically newest schema-valid receipt for a version; treats a receipt whose `skill_id` or `version` disagrees with its path as ABSENT; returns the committed run ids for a version; never writes and never spawns a fetch.
batches.syncRule: Read-only over committed files. The version key is the 40-char lowercase tree hash, resolved with `latestTree` (readme.ts:119-122) or `skillVersions` (S7d) — never the 8-char `LsSkill.latest`, which `shortHash` (readme.ts:224) truncates and which is unusable as a directory key.

verification.corrections:
S7n is CHANGED per the delta (nothing of EV-13/CP-11/CP-15/IB-02 landed in the 18 commits), and the batch already honours the important half of that change by delivering the reader as a `receipt` VERB rather than an exported reader — that is correct and should stand. Nine material problems remain.

1. SEAM DTO BREAK — the batch's central unaddressed gap. `receipts(q:{skillId;version}):Promise<Result<Receipt|null>>` (desktop/src/backend/Backend.ts:9) where `Receipt = NonNullable<Design['DETAIL']['receipt']>` (desktop/src/backend/types.ts:15). That fixture object has 24 keys: abstract, arm, attribution, catalog, cc, coverage, date, eff, efficiency_text, engine, inc_p, incumbent, judge, k, model, per_case, results, run_id, runner, sign_p, timestamp, trigger_text, triggers, when. The CLI's receiptSchema (src/lib/evals/receipt.ts:50-93) has NONE of abstract/results/trigger_text/efficiency_text/coverage/catalog/incumbent/inc_p/eff/per_case/when/date; it nests model/judge_model/cc_version/engine_version/k/runner_handle under `provenance`; and `sign_p` is a NUMBER per arm inside `comparisons`, not a top-level string. So a `latestReceipt()` that returns a schema-valid CLI receipt CANNOT satisfy `receipts()`. The batch names no DTO change, no adapter mapping, no prose-synthesis rule — and its own §12 paragraph (b) forbids the app inventing them. Either the seam's `Receipt` narrows to what the CLI actually stores (a boards consequence for §6), or the batch must state where the five prose blocks and the display triples come from. As written the batch cannot land.

2. `receipts()` HAS ZERO UI CONSUMERS TODAY, so "read through the seam's `receipts()` instead of the fixture" is a rewire, not a swap. grep for `receipts(` over desktop/src excluding src/backend returns nothing. The evals rail and report read `SkillDetail` from `skill()`: SkillScreen.tsx:41 renders `<EvaluationReport name={s.name} version={s.version} receipt={s.receipt} summary={s.summary} incumbentLift={s.incumbentLift} numbers={s.reportNumbers} method={s.method}/>` plus `<HistoryRail history={s.history}/>`, and DetailRail (SkillScreen.tsx:23) reads `rc.when`, `rc.runner`, `rc.model`, `rc.cc`, `rc.k`. summary / history[].summary / reportNumbers / incumbentLift / method are SkillDetail-only derived fields that `receipts()` does not return, and `skill()` is still `gap('Skill detail')` (desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:65). The evals surface therefore cannot become real from S7n alone — undeclared dependency on S7p.

3. THE MARKETPLACE DEFAULT-OFF IS NOT AN APP-SIDE CHANGE, and it breaks an existing test. `catalog.filterDefault` is `design.FILTER_DEFAULT` verbatim (mock/data.ts:25); design.json is written only by `python3 tools/export-design.py` from the design canvas and is never hand-edited (desktop/AGENTS.md invariant 3). Today FILTER_DEFAULT = {verdicts:['PASS'], lift_min:20, tokens_max:5.0, installs_min:3} and DERIVED.filterCount = 6. market-filters.tsx:12 seeds the verdict checkboxes from `catalog.filterDefault.verdicts` and :14 seeds the three Sliders from lift_min/tokens_max/installs_min with a footer button reading `Show {catalog.filterCount} skills`. marketplace.test.tsx:13 asserts `getByRole('checkbox',{name:/PASS/})` IS CHECKED and the button reads `Show ${design.DERIVED.filterCount} skills`. So "ships with a zero badge and no active facets on first run" requires a build.py/design-canvas change (Teddy), a .shots re-lock of MarketplaceFilters at tolerance screen 0.0030, and an update to that test. Approver "Ajay" alone is wrong for this row.

4. "Delete GAPS.md:40" IS THE WRONG LINE AND THE WRONG ACTOR. GAPS.md:40 is MarketplaceFilters — "`search` is skills-only substring over the clone; no facet filtering. Filters are app-side over the catalog." S7n adds no CLI-side facet filtering and paragraph (a) deliberately KEEPS the filter viewer-set and app-side, so the gap that line records is not closed. Separately, desktop/AGENTS.md:23-28 states "an implementing agent never edits `GAPS.md`, `FIDELITY.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` or `package.json` — describe what you found in the report's `openQuestions`/`deviations` instead", so instructing the Codex run to delete a GAPS line breaks the repo's own rule. For reference GAPS.md carries no receipt-reader bullet at all; the receipt-adjacent lines are :20 (receipt-check as a hidden CI verb, "no seam method, no screen"), :44 (12-char hashes) and :49 (no --json mode). The real maintainer edit here is re-anchoring GAPS.md:1, which still reads "pinned at b5c0507".

5. THREE MISSING CLI/ADAPTER EDITS, all forced by the shipped frame protocol. (a) The new verb must join `FRAME_VERBS` (src/lib/frames.ts:32) or a shell cannot discover it in the hello frame — that list is 20 entries today, not the 21 the delta states (login, setup, team create/join/remove/leave/workflow-update, invite, ls, status, publish, validate, eval, connect, install, uninstall-skill, uninstall, sync, search, update). (b) It needs a `CliVerbs` slot so it is injectable in tests, the pattern `app?` follows at src/cli.ts:34-37. (c) The adapter must replace `receipts: async () => gap('Eval receipts')` (desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:66) with a real mapping plus a `.passthrough()` cliReceipt schema beside the twelve at index.ts:17-30. None of the three is in cliChanges.

6. ZERO-PROMPT IS A HARD CONSTRAINT, NOT AN IMPLICATION. `read()` iterates the frames and on ANY ask cancels the process and fails with 'terum-skills asked "<question>" during a read-only call…' (desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:46-53). "Read-only, never fetches, never writes" does not by itself guarantee prompt-free: the batch must say how `receipt` resolves a multi-team config without asking (the `--team` question other verbs raise), and the tests line should assert it emits no ask frame.

7. THE READER IS THREE FUNCTIONS, SO THE "CANNOT DRIFT" CLAIM IS HALF TRUE. readme.ts has `latestReceiptVerdict` (filesystem, :172-181, called at :137), `latestReceiptVerdictInTree` (MutableTree, :184-190, called at :166 — the safeWrite post-image fallback), and the shared `receiptVerdict` (:192-200) which is where the skill_id/version-vs-path rule and the partial rule (:197-199) actually live. A single `latestReceipt(clone, skillId, version)` signature serves the fs caller only; the in-tree caller reads a post-image and cannot take a clone path. Factor the shared VALIDATOR and keep two enumerators, or the safeWrite path silently keeps its own copy of the rule.

8. dependsOn IS INCOMPLETE (S7m itself is right). S7m is a correct serialization edge — validate/receipt-check/eval sit at src/cli.ts:115/116/117 and both batches work src/lib/evals/. Two edges are missing: (i) syncRule depends on `skillVersions (S7d)` for the 40-char tree-hash key, and S7d is itself CHANGED by the delta (its RM-10/RM-22/CP-35 exported readers are moot as exports and must be rebuilt as verb payloads), so `skillVersions` may not exist in the form cited; (ii) the appHalf depends on S7p per finding 2. No re-pointing is needed for the retired library-entry batch — S7n does not depend on S7a.

9. ANCHOR DRIFT + A NAMING HAZARD. The risk's citation "cli.ts:116" was correct at b5c0507 (eval was 116 there, receipt-check 115) but at cli-main f8557c4 the file shifted: 115 validate, 116 receipt-check, 117 `program.command('eval <skill>')`. The underlying risk claim is sound and worth keeping. Two adjacent hazards it does not mention: the new public verb `receipt` sits one hyphen from the existing hidden `receipt-check` (cli.ts:116), and the proposed `src/lib/evals/receipts.ts` sits one letter from the existing `src/lib/evals/receipt.ts` (with `__tests__/receipt.test.ts` already present) — pick distinct names.

TESTS AND SIZE. `src/lib/evals/__tests__/receipts.test.ts` fits the CLI layout exactly (that directory already holds ten files: agent/checks/execution/generate/hygiene/judge/receipt/results/stats/triggers.test.ts), and the four assertions are all describable there against the injected Runner. The desktop half names no test though both layouts exist: colocated (desktop/src/screens/marketplace/marketplace.test.tsx) and __tests__ (desktop/src/backend/tauri/__tests__/run.test.ts) — add an adapter test at desktop/src/backend/tauri/__tests__/ and update marketplace.test.tsx:13 if finding 3 survives. On "one Codex run + one PR": CLI and app are one repo now (desktop/ inside terum-skills), so one PR is mechanically possible, but the batch spans four owners — CLI code (Ryan), app code (agent), the design canvas FILTER_DEFAULT + a board re-lock (Teddy), and three §12 eval-engine paragraphs (Ajay) whose home is not this repo at all (cli-main has no specs/, only docs/frame-protocol.md). Split the §12 paragraphs and the filter default out; the residue — shared validator, `receipt` verb, FRAME_VERBS/CliVerbs entries, adapter mapping — is genuinely size S.

D20: no violation. A viewer-set marketplace facet is per-viewer by construction and is never rendered as a team-wide fact, and the batch adds no localStorage-backed team-wide claim. The seam rule (AGENTS.md invariant 1) is also respected — the work stays inside src/backend/ and the CLI — except for the GAPS.md edit in finding 4.

VERDICT: the batch's anchors all exist and are byte-stable, but the batch as written BREAKS the costed SIMPLE bar on its central sentence, undercounts the existing readers, and — post-delta — has no delivery mechanism, no team selector, and a seam key mismatch. Nine corrections, one of them disqualifying.

ANCHORS THAT VERIFY (read this session in cli-clone; all three files are byte-identical at 85cc276 and at today's f8557c4 — `git diff --stat 85cc276..HEAD -- src/lib/readme.ts src/commands/receiptCheck.ts src/lib/version.ts src/lib/evals/receipt.ts src/lib/config.ts` is empty):
- `latestReceiptVerdict` at src/lib/readme.ts:172-181, and it is exactly the rule the batch describes (readdir, `.filter(name => name.endsWith('.json')).sort().at(-1)`, ENOENT→undefined, then validate).
- The path-vs-content check and the fail-open catch at src/lib/readme.ts:192-200 (`if (!receipt.success || receipt.data.skill_id.toLowerCase() !== id.toLowerCase() || receipt.data.version !== version) return undefined;` … `catch { return undefined; }`), with the partial rule at :196-199.
- `latestTree` at src/lib/readme.ts:119-122; `shortHash` at src/lib/readme.ts:224 (8 chars).
- `resolveVersion` at src/lib/version.ts:9-28.
- The RISK is correct and independently confirmed: `program.command('eval <skill>')` binds its positional (cli.ts:116 @ 85cc276), and the costing adds a second reason — `eval show` is on the Out/deferred list at .planning/specs/2026-09-02-phase-1-build.md:24 (costing:601).

1. DISQUALIFYING — "factored out so the README column, CI and the UI cannot drift" inverts the costing's own scope rule and breaks the SIMPLE bar. EV-13's costed body (costing:601, "Verb or flag") says in capitals: "CRITICAL SCOPE RULE: do NOT rewire src/lib/readme.ts or src/commands/receiptCheck.ts onto it in this change — their fail-open vs fail-closed behaviours differ on purpose and re-pointing either one would change the README column or the publish gate, dragging in a second spec section (.planning/specs/2026-09-04-eval-engine.md section 6.1 :289 and section 11 :470-476) and breaking condition (5)." Its "Why SIMPLE" repeats the conditional: "SIMPLE holds only with the scope rule above … the coster's 'extract once and have readme.ts call it' is NOT a free refactor." I verified the divergence in the clone: readme.ts:200 swallows a malformed newest receipt (`catch { return undefined; }`, README prints a dash) while src/commands/receiptCheck.ts:104-107 THROWS (`schema-invalid receipt <path>: invalid JSON.` / `schema-invalid receipt <path>.`), with the reason stated in its docstring at receiptCheck.ts:91 ("A malformed newest file fails closed rather than hiding behind an older run"); receiptCheck.ts:94 also filters `entry.isFile()` where readme.ts:177 does not. The batch's own prose is self-contradictory here — it asserts a single factored reader AND that "the UI shows no receipt while CI still blocks the publish", which the same helper cannot do without a mode parameter and two callers rewired. FIX: state that src/lib/evals/receipts.ts is NEW and ADDITIVE, that readme.ts and receiptCheck.ts are deliberately NOT re-pointed, and add the two regression tests the costing lists and the batch omits — `src/lib/__tests__/readme.test.ts: existing cases stay green` and `src/commands/__tests__/receiptCheck.test.ts: existing cases stay green`. Drop "so the README column, CI and the UI cannot drift"; the honest claim is "so the UI does not add a fifth divergent copy".

2. Reader count is wrong: it is the FIFTH, not the fourth. The costing flags this as "the coster's most materially stale paragraph and both refuters caught it" (costing:600): at b5c0507 there are already four private ones — latestReceiptVerdict (readme.ts:172-181), latestReceiptVerdictInTree (readme.ts:184-190), receiptVerdict (readme.ts:192-201), and receiptCheck.ts's receiptFiles/newestReceiptAt/hasSchemaValidReceipt (:92-97, :100-109, :111-119, all confirmed in the clone) — plus two cross-version walkers, latestReceiptedTree (src/commands/eval.ts:252-267) and validReceiptsOutsideVersion (receiptCheck.ts:121-129). Note also that the costing's own paste-ready §12 paragraph still says "It is a third reader of the same rule" (costing:605); whichever number S7n lands, the spec text and the batch text must agree.

3. POST-DELTA, the batch has no delivery mechanism. The costed verb PRINTS the receipt as JSON via `io.print`. Over frames a print is a `print` frame, and the adapter reads only `result.value` (desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:47-53 `read()`, and the map applied to the parsed value). So EV-13 must put the receipt (and the run-id list) on the verb's Result VALUE, not on stdout — the delta says exactly this for S7n. Additive under protocol 1 (docs/frame-protocol.md:61-63). Add it to cliChanges explicitly; without it the app gets a print frame it is not allowed to parse and `receipts()` stays gapped.

4. POST-DELTA, the new verb must be registered in FRAME_VERBS. src/lib/frames.ts:32 @ f8557c4 lists 20 verbs and deliberately excludes hidden maintenance verbs — which is why `receipt-check` is absent. A `receipt` verb that is not added there is never advertised in the hello frame. Same edit S7l and S7z already carry; S7n's cliChanges omits it. (Aside for the delta record: that list has 20 entries, not the 21 the delta fact `hello-frame-payload` states.)

5. The verb signature drops `--team`, and that is a hard failure on a multi-team machine. The costing's registration includes `.option('--team <team>', 'configured team (required when more than one exists)')` (costing:601); the batch's is `receipt <ref> [--skill-version <tree>] [--runs]`. `selectTeam` (src/lib/config.ts:23-30) THROWS `More than one team is configured; pass --team <name> (…)` and never prompts — good for the adapter's read(), which cancels on any ask (index.ts:50), but it means `receipts()` hard-fails for anyone with two teams, and the adapter passes no `--team` on any call today.

6. Seam key mismatch, and the seam's Receipt is not the CLI's receipt. `receipts(q: { skillId: string; version: string })` (desktop/src/backend/Backend.ts:9) keys on the receipt path's uuid, while the verb takes `<ref>` (a skill name, as install/eval do). Either the verb must accept a uuid ref or the adapter needs a uuid→name map that no verb returns (RM-30/ls territory). Separately, the seam's `Receipt | null` is the fixture-shaped DISPLAY object (abstract, results, trigger_text, efficiency_text, coverage, sign_p as a string, arm/eff triples), none of which exist in receiptSchema (src/lib/evals/receipt.ts:50-93) — so the appHalf's "the evals rail and report read through the seam's receipts() instead of the fixture" is not closed by EV-13 alone. Today the adapter hard-gaps it (`receipts: async () => gap('Eval receipts')`, desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:66) and returns `receipt: null` from eval (:82).

7. "Delete GAPS.md:40" is premature and points at another batch's row. Verified: desktop/GAPS.md:40 is the MarketplaceFilters line ("verdict / lift / tokens / installs facets, default 4 active"), and costing §8:1859 maps it to CP-11, CP-15 AND RM-38. RM-38 ("'Recently updated' sort has no field: nothing in the read model carries a last-changed date", costing:84) is in S7f, and S7n declares no dependsOn edge to it. Also: after the fold-in the live file is desktop/GAPS.md in the CLI repo (line 40 byte-identical to the app-repo copy), and its header is still anchored at b5c0507 — and EV-13 itself has NO GAPS.md line, so the receipts() gap this batch actually closes is not recorded there.

8. syncRule cites a stale name and an undeclared, now-moot dependency. `skillVersions (S7d)` is RM-10, whose costed title is "Export the batched skillTrees reader" (costing:76) — skillTrees, not skillVersions — and per the delta S7d's exported-reader half is MOOT (an export the app can never import); dependsOn lists only S7m. Re-point to whatever verb payload replaces RM-10, or drop the alternative: `latestTree` (readme.ts:119-122) plus `resolveVersion` (version.ts:9-28) already suffice. One refinement to the syncRule's own claim: resolveVersion DOES accept a short display prefix and normalises it to the lowercase 40-char tree (version.ts:11-20, rejecting a 39-char truncation explicitly), so the verb may accept the short form even though the DIRECTORY key must be the full 40-char hash.

9. Two costed constraints the batch silently drops, both app-facing:
   (a) The verb must NOT call refreshClone (costing:601): refreshClone fetches and `reset --hard origin/main` inside the clone WRITER lock (src/lib/teamRepo.ts:462), so a UI read that called it would hard-reset the working tree on every render — the D-R4 hazard. "Never fetches, never writes" implies it; name it, because this verb is called on every skill-detail render.
   (b) The module may not live in src/lib/evals/receipt.ts, whose header declares it "Pure (ME1): no I/O" (receipt.ts:4) — which is the real reason for the new `receipts.ts`. Flag the one-letter filename adjacency (receipt.ts vs receipts.ts) and the verb-name adjacency (`receipt` beside the existing hidden `receipt-check`, cli.ts:116 @ f8557c4) as naming hazards; commander does not prefix-match, so neither is a parse bug.

10. Test list is thinner than the costed one: missing "returns undefined for a version with no receipt directory (ENOENT is not an error)", the runIds ordering/filtering case, and the two command-level cases in src/commands/__tests__/receipt.test.ts ("prints the latest receipt … and runs no git fetch"; "fails clearly for an unknown skill, an unknown version, and a version with no receipt"). The batch folds "never spawns a fetch" into the lib test file, where it cannot be observed.

11. Line-number drift at today's main (f8557c4): cli.ts:116 (eval's positional) is now cli.ts:117 — validate :115, receipt-check :116, eval :117 — because 898a795/c487048 moved the region. Every other anchor S7n cites is unmoved.

NOT a problem, for the record: no team.json row, no guard change, no owner file at all (read-only, no safeWrite/GuardAction/PEOPLE_ACTIONS entry) — the batch is right that the SIMPLE bar's owner-file and verb-count conditions hold; the bar breaks only on correction 1 (spec sections) unless the scope rule is restored. batches.title: SKILL.md body and the hand-maintained project fields
batches.cliChanges: `src/lib/schema.ts` — `parseSkillFrontmatter`'s success shape gains `body: string`, the bytes after the closing `---`, split at the existing FRONTMATTER match the function ALREADY computes, so the boundary reaches a consumer as a value rather than as a regex a second reader has to reproduce; `SkillRecord` (src/lib/skills.ts:7-14, today `{id, name, team, directory, frontmatter, grants}`) carries it, and `skillAtSource` (install.ts:156) must set it from the source IT parsed, so a record built from a materialized pinned version never carries the clone's prose. No file gains a field, no parse rule changes, CRLF and a missing trailing newline behave as today, a file with no frontmatter still behaves, and the enumerator does no extra I/O because the file is already read in full. This deliberately does NOT unify the three sibling helpers that each re-implement the same boundary with their own literal (`declaredCategory` skills.ts:121, `injectManagedFields` skills.ts:139, `canonicalSkillMd`) — that unification is a separate change and is not proposed. The `projects` object stays hand-maintained on the host through GitHub's own editor — no verb creates or removes a project key, `publish --project` refuses a key that is not already present, `team create` scaffolds `projects: {}`, and a clone push carrying that change is refused by the pre-push guard. The declared-key route is therefore NOT taken; if Teddy wants a curated sentence instead, it is a COPY CONVENTION for description, not a schema change. All three edges are serialization only. Placing it last costs nothing, because the body is a rendering input rather than a dependency of any other row.
batches.risk: `skillAtSource` is the subtle half: if `body` is set from the clone's working copy rather than the materialized pinned tree, a pinned placement's detail page shows prose the placed copy does not have. The test must cover a pinned version explicitly.

batches.cliChanges: NONE — and that is the point of the batch. Seven of the nine change nothing in the CLI at all; the costing corrects an earlier draft that called them "buildable as one PR" with "there is no PR for them to be buildable as; they are spec records or frontend rules". AC-07 and CP-14's `team.json` route is REFUSED, not merely unbuilt: AC-07's field would turn `categories: z.array(z.string())` (schema.ts:46) into a union carrying `{key, icon}` and CP-14's project-metadata route would need `team project --remote/--rename`, and both need a NEW permitted-writes row, while `guardTeam` admits exactly three shapes and nothing else (guard.ts:150-157: row c `publish` + `onlySkillListsChanged`, row d `team-remove` + `archivedAppendedOnly`, row e `join` + `archivedRemovedOnly`) and no verb owns writing `team.json.categories` after `team create`. Their refusals are recorded here so nobody re-asks.
batches.appHalf: All nine, plus the flag contract this batch must repair. AC-06: the three-mode window chrome as a frontend-spec paragraph (D-W2) — macOS `decorations:true`, `titleBarStyle:'Overlay'`, `hiddenTitle:true`, `trafficLightPosition {x:16,y:14}` as a LOGICAL position so the OS lights land on exactly the pixels the design drew and the mark stays at x 76; Windows/Linux `decorations:false`, no lights, mark at x 16, and a 138 px (3×46) reserve that re-lays BOTH end blocks rather than insetting one; browser/mock keeps the drawn cosmetic dots, which is what the fidelity baselines contain; dragging is `data-tauri-drag-region` on empty regions only (it does not inherit to children) with double-click-to-maximise hand-built, and `decorations:false` gives NO resize border, so 4-6 px edge and corner targets calling `startResizeDragging()` are a build item, not a test note. REQUIRED GATE CARVE-OUT: the fidelity gate runs browser mode, so both platform headers ship untested by it — either mask the top-bar left block and test chrome separately, or state that the gate's coverage stops at the panel edge. AC-08: four calls behind one seam — `revealPath`, `openInEditor`, `openUrl`, `copyToClipboard` — over `tauri-plugin-opener` (`opener:allow-open-path`, `opener:allow-open-url`, each with its own scope) and `tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager` (`clipboard-manager:allow-write-text`, none enabled by default), with `window.open`/`navigator.clipboard.writeText` in the browser build; the repo link must be COMPUTED (`https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/tree/<commit>/skills/<name>/`) because every drawn anchor is `href="#"`; `openPath` opens the OS default handler, not an editor, so either the label changes or an editor preference is added; and `user-select:none` must come off content, because the copy button is currently the only way to get a command string out of the window. AC-07: a deterministic category-key→glyph derivation WITH a fallback, app-side — an icon is presentation, and putting it in the committed team file to make a glyph appear is the dishonest direction. CP-14: Edit opens the authored source (`config.shared[id].source`, schema.ts:97) or is hidden; a placed copy is generated output, so the sync warning must sit next to that button. CP-13: draw the consequence dialog for `uninstall-skill project|member` writing `declined`. IB-08: give the three counters ("Needs attention 8", sidebar Alerts 8, sidebar Updates 3) ONE shared definition; the two scans they consume are EV-19's and RM-39's and are costed there. RM-27: render `ghState` (auth.ts:21) as-is; sign-in stays a terminal hand-off, because `auth.ts:44` is the only `stdio:'inherit'` spawn in non-test source and gh's device-code flow needs a real terminal — nothing in terum-skills runs `gh auth logout` or a package manager. RM-45: render `explainGitAccessFailure`'s text verbatim as SELECTABLE text with a copy button on the `gh auth setup-git --hostname github.com` line, and ship NO fix-it button and NO probe — spec:336 forbids all four, and on the `sync` path the app must capture the Prompter's PRINT stream, not the failure string, because a non-hook sync's message says "See the notices above". RM-47: SIX surfaces, not five — the five `CloneState` arms (`absent`, `incomplete/not-a-repository`, `incomplete/no-team-json`, `incomplete/unverifiable`, `foreign`) plus a per-team read failure with `clone.state === 'ok'` and `readable: false`, which status.ts:88-89 produces and the drawn ShareError depicts; and `absent` does NOT mean "another window left this team", because a completed `team leave` deletes the config entry and `status` iterates `config.teams` (status.ts:33), so a left team VANISHES from the payload — the cross-window-leave signal is a diff of two StatusResults. THE ONE BUG THIS BATCH MUST FIX: the five capability flags have ZERO consumers anywhere in the app today. Only `windowChrome` is read (`desktop/src/components/domain/Shell.tsx:15` queries `backend.capabilities()` and :20 passes it to `TopBar`, plus `OnboardingParts.tsx:15-16`); `disablePerMachine`, `inboxEventLog`, `offtargetKind`, `machineRegistry` and `perCaseEvalTables` are consumed by nothing outside `src/backend/`. So a `false` from a real adapter changes no pixel and M6's exit criterion — "capability flags flip from the adapter" — is unobservable. Wire each flag to its surface, or the contract is decorative.

batches.rationale: The single app-only batch the rules allow. Most of these rows are already SHIPPED by the M1-M4 loop as drawn — the app renders every affordance on the mock and 87/87 boards are pixel-locked — so this batch is mostly writing down the boundary that already holds (which store owns what, which values are per-machine, which derivations are permitted) plus the four adapter rules that can be built against the mock today and handed to M6.
batches.risk: `print` and `progress` frames are produced and DISCARDED today: `driveRun` (desktop/src/backend/drive.ts:7-12) iterates `run.frames` and acts ONLY on `frame.t === 'ask'`, and nothing outside `src/backend/` consumes `.frames`. So RM-17's progress work has no consumer until this batch adds one, and the drawn progress phases are currently decorative. Also: none of this may hand-edit the generated fixture or move a pixel.
batches.tests: `theme.test.ts` (five cases), `prefs` round-trip with an unreadable store yielding drawn defaults, the ported contrast gate over the app's tokens, an Inbox recomputation test proving no timer and no `sync --hook` call, a single-flight queue test proving at most one mutating verb in flight, and a Prompter test proving the gh offer is answered `false`. Gate: `npm run check` in `desktop/`.
batches.syncRule: The one rule that binds every app row: the app must NEVER sync on a timer, because an app-initiated sync writes `run/<team>.stamp` (sync.ts:348) and thereby suppresses the SessionStart hook's own sync for the next hour (sync.ts:130 + hook.ts:149). Refresh is subscribe-push + revalidate-on-visible + a low-frequency poll of the two cheap local reads + an explicit Sync now, with invalidation keyed by source (config, clone:<team>, placed, stamp:<team>) and NO optimistic cache writes for any CLI-backed mutation, because `install` writes its `pending` entry before placement (install.ts:90-92) and a failed install leaves durable state the next read shows.

verification.corrections:
S7s is CHANGED, not DONE or MOOT: nothing in the 27-commit delta (b5c0507..85cc276) or the 18-commit delta to f8557c4 touches quarantine writing or adds any measurement, and both owner files it names are byte-identical between b5c0507 and 85cc276 (src/lib/placer.ts IDENTICAL, src/commands/leave.ts IDENTICAL, src/commands/status.ts IDENTICAL; only src/commands/uninstallMachine.ts DIFF, via 1f87b52, +18/-3 for the /terum-skills wrapper rows — the sweep list itself unchanged). Six corrections, the first two load-bearing.

(1) FALSE PREMISE, and it is the sentence the whole CP-S1 half rests on. "moveToQuarantine (src/lib/placer.ts:170) is the SINGLE funnel" is wrong at 85cc276 and was wrong at b5c0507. `teardownTeam` builds its quarantine destination inline and never calls the helper: src/commands/leave.ts:99-105 does `const stamp = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-'); const destination = join(store.root, 'quarantine', stamp, `teams-${name}`); await mkdir(dirname(destination), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 }); await moveDirectory(clone, destination);` — a duplicated copy of the timestamp rule calling moveDirectory (placer.ts:186) directly. It is reached from TWO verbs: `leave` (leave.ts:41) and `uninstall` (uninstallMachine.ts:111). The real map is six write sites through two funnels: install.ts:116, placer.ts:106, placer.ts:121, placer.ts:161 (the quarantineDrift path used by sync.ts:266 and uninstall.ts:131 via remove()), connect.ts:421 — all through moveToQuarantine — plus leave.ts:101, which is not. The costing inherited the same error (costing:199 and :1306 both say "all five call sites funnel through one helper, src/lib/placer.ts:170") while its own body at :1306 simultaneously names leave.ts:101's `teams-<name>` entry as a specimen. Consequences for the batch: its own cliChanges lists "a team leave clone" as one of the three reasons the sidecar must record, and that is precisely the path the funnel does not cover; the fix is either a behaviour-preserving refactor of teardownTeam onto moveToQuarantine (same stamp rule, same 0700 mkdir, same moveDirectory, plus a reason argument) or two write sites; and `tests` must gain leave.test.ts (clone-with-unpushed-work quarantined WITH its reason) and uninstallMachine coverage, since teardownTeam is shared. The stated size M assumed one helper edit; it is now placer + leave + status.

(2) CP-S1's COSTED RECOMMENDATION IS THE DESIGN FIX, AND THIS BATCH SILENTLY OVERTURNS IT. The row's cells are `CP-S1 | MEDIUM | SIMPLE (ok) | design | Ryan` (costing:199) — CLI MEDIUM, design SIMPLE, recommended owner design — and its rationale ends "...hence MEDIUM rather than HARD — and it is not needed: the recommended fix is design-side and costs nothing" (costing:199, :1306). §8.1 counts CP-S1 in the 39 `SIMPLE · design` rows (costing:1879). S7s adopts the rejected MEDIUM CLI route without recording that it reverses a costed call. Either state the reversal explicitly in the batch and put it to Ryan as such, or drop CP-S1 back to design-side and let S7s carry MC-S1 alone — which is a strictly stronger version of the batch's own escape hatch, since it removes the new-state-file breach of SIMPLE condition (1) as well as condition (5).

(3) MC-S1's DESIGN-SIDE HALF IS HARD AND IS ABSENT FROM THE BATCH. The row is `MC-S1 | MEDIUM | HARD (ok) | cli | Ryan` (costing:229) — the HARD is the design cost, and §4's body says why (costing:1683): four always-settled rows (build.py:3654 Sync▸Quarantine, :3710 Evals▸Run trees, :3757/:3758 Advanced▸Pinned checkouts and Eval runs) are drawn as finished strings that "a recursive walk cannot fill instantly — the 312 MB eval tree is the slow one", so the design must either add a per-row pending "—" (the vocabulary already exists at build.py:3762) or move sizes behind the Diagnostics Run button. S7s's appHalf says only that the rows "render real bytes", names no latency treatment, and its approver line names two Ryan-owned prose sections while the HARD change is Teddy's build.py. Under the delta this gets worse, not better: every read is one spawned `node <entry> --frames status` process (desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:39-49) driven by read() (desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:47-53), so the walk blocks the whole Settings read with no partial frame — ProgressFrame exists but is emitted by no verb (src/lib/frames.ts:22).

(4) DELTA — the app half must name its seam method, and it is settings(), not status(). Both are gapped by the shipped adapter (desktop/src/backend/tauri/index.ts:61 status, :62 settings), and the drawn Settings ▸ Machine's storage / quarantine card is served by settings(). Putting a `storage` block on the `status` verb payload is fine on the CLI side but the batch must say which Backend method consumes it or the block lands where nothing renders it. Two things do go the batch's way here: src/commands/status.ts contains no io.confirm/io.text/io.select, so it is legal on read()'s prompt-free path (index.ts:46-53 cancels on any ask), and `status` is already in FRAME_VERBS (src/lib/frames.ts:32), so adding a result field is additive with no protocol bump (docs/frame-protocol.md:61-63).

(5) The rationale's impossibility claim is stale and understates itself. "the documented Tauri fs plugin surface has no size or metadata call" — at f8557c4 the shell ships no fs plugin at all: the Rust half is 151 lines exposing exactly five commands, cli_spawn / cli_write / cli_kill / read_app_state / host_platform (desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:36-37, :137-140), plus opener, store, clipboard-manager and window-state. Re-word to "the shell exposes no filesystem command whatsoever", which makes the CLI route the only route rather than merely the preferred one.

(6) Scope of the storage set. The costed mechanism names three paths the CLI already constructs, all verified: cache/ at src/lib/version.ts:36, evals/ at src/commands/eval.ts:111 (costing cites :103 @ b5c0507 — line drift only, the b5c0507 blob has the identical statement at :103), quarantine/ at src/commands/sync.ts:500 (costing cites :361 @ b5c0507 — same drift). S7s adds a fourth, teams/, which is the largest tree on disk (git clones) and is not a drawn Settings row; meanwhile store.root also holds backups/ (uninstallMachine.ts:44) and run/, which neither the batch's set nor §4.2's sweep covers. Drop teams/ or say why it is measured.

Two smaller things to fold in, both new:
(a) Sidecar naming collision. moveToQuarantine's directory is millisecond-stamped and `mkdir(..., {recursive:true})` never fails on an existing dir (placer.ts:171-173), and sync.ts:266 quarantines inside a loop over placements, so two moves in the same millisecond share one `<timestamp>/` directory. A single `reason.json` "beside the moved folder" would then be overwritten by the second mover, attributing the wrong reason to both. Make it per-folder — `<name>.reason.json` — not one per timestamp directory.
(b) The prune test claim holds, with a Windows caveat that now matters. prune reads entries immediately under the quarantine root and does `rm(path, {recursive:true, force:false})` (sync.ts:498-511), so a sidecar inside `<timestamp>/` is deleted with its folder — the batch's sync.test.ts assertion is sound. But the guard on that list is `paths.filter((path) => path.startsWith(`${root}/`))` (sync.ts:504), a POSIX separator against a `resolve()`d path, so on Windows every entry is filtered out and prune reports "Quarantine is empty." syncDesign:
## What "more intelligent sync" must actually do — and the correction to Teddy's premise

**The load-bearing finding: a new `people/<handle>.json` field propagates today with ZERO sync code.** Teddy's premise ("nearly everything is low cost simply by updating the metadata... with more intelligent sync") is right about the metadata and needs LESS than he thinks from sync. Mechanism, verified line by line this session:

1. **Propagation in.** Each team's per-team pass hard-resets its clone to `origin/main` (`refreshClone(runner, clone, {...})`, src/commands/sync.ts:147). Every subsequent read of a person file goes through `personSchema`, which sync imports at sync.ts:15 and which is `.passthrough()` (src/lib/schema.ts:64). So an unknown field survives the parse.
2. **Propagation is not clobbered by sync's own writes.** Sync's ONLY people-file writes are the two orphan-pass `safeWrite`s: adopt parses the pre-image with `parseJson(personSchema, treeText(raw), personPath)` at sync.ts:388, pushes onto `installed`, and re-serializes the WHOLE parsed object with `JSON.stringify(fresh, null, 2)` at sync.ts:392; decline does the same onto `declined` at sync.ts:402/:406. Neither reconstructs the object, so `role`, `projects` (S7b) and any future person field ride through untouched.
3. **Therefore** a field written on machine A by `profile` reaches machine B at B's next sync with no sync change at all. The "more intelligent sync" is the four small things below, not a propagation engine.

## Derivations at sync time — the honest set, and the forbidden set

**Permitted, because every input is committed and every number is the CLI's own answer:** install counts (`installCounts`, src/lib/readme.ts:40 — this IS D38's definition, so the app must not mint a parallel one); project membership counts and facepiles (a group-by over `people/*.json.projects` once S7b lands, never stored, so `team.json` gains no members array); per-skill health (S7g's three-fingerprint compare, read-only — `quarantineDrift` at sync.ts:266 remains the only thing that ACTS on a local-changed answer); last-changed dates (`git log -1 --format=%cI -- skills/<name>`, S7f); joined dates (`git log --diff-filter=A --reverse -- people/<handle>.json`, S7b's app half); the Inbox item set (recomputed from clone + `config.pending` + `config.placements` + `evals/`, S7r).

**Forbidden, with the reason each is not a sync feature:**
- **An event log.** No store exists, and neither owner file can hold per-session rows. IB-03 needs a collector, a log, a SECOND SessionStart hook entry (whose idempotency key is "a hook command containing terum-skills inside any SessionStart group", so a differently-triggered hook is a new mechanism, not an increment) and a privacy call over the user's literal prompts — four NOT-SIMPLE triggers at once, behind a scope non-goal. Recommended CUT.
- **A machine registry.** Verified by grep over `src` (excluding tests): `hostname()` appears exactly ONCE in non-test source, as a lock-owner token in `acquireTeamLock` (src/lib/hook.ts:190). There is no machine identity anywhere. Cross-machine propagation IS `people/<you>.json.installed` (entries are `{id, version, scope, since}`, schema.ts:36-41, where scope is global|project and never a machine) replayed by sync per machine. A real registry needs a new committed path plus a new permitted-writes row, and `guardTeam` is closed to rows c/d/e (guard.ts:150-157).
- **Last-seen as a heartbeat.** The only artifact is the machine-local `run/<team>.stamp` (hook.ts:157), never committed. PF-05's honest route is relabelling the column "Last active" over committed history.

## Conflict rules

Two writers of one person file cannot collide destructively: every write goes through `repo.safeWrite`, which re-applies the mutation against a freshly fetched pre-image and re-runs `guard` INSIDE the loop (openTeamRepo/safeWrite, teamRepo.ts:86-90; called at sync.ts:385 and :398), so a concurrent teammate's `profile --role` is not lost — the mutation is replayed on top of it. Across handles there is no shared row to conflict on at all, because guard row (b) (guard.ts:49) confines every actor to `people/<their-handle>.json`. Same-handle-two-machines is last-writer-wins per FIELD, which is correct for a self-declared label. `projects[]` names must be validated against `team.json` read from the PRE-IMAGE tree inside the mutation, or a concurrent `publish` (the one verb permitted to change `projects[].skills`, guard row c) makes the check stale.

RM-31 needs no `stamped` field. The remainder is one line: drop the `args.hook ?` ternary at sync.ts:353 and :359. **Proven safe:** `createExecute` routes hook notices only when `isHookSync(value)` holds, requiring `hook === true` AND both arrays (src/lib/execute.ts:24, :42-44), and `hook: Boolean(args.hook)` keeps the discriminant accurate.

## Hook behaviour — the one thing that must not change

`sync --hook` is typed to a print-only `NonInteractivePrompter` (sync.ts:41-42, :62-63), stdout carries only `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","reloadSkills":true}}` (sync.ts:327), notices ride `SyncResult.notices` to stderr, and a team stamped within the hour is SILENTLY skipped (`stampIsFresh`, sync.ts:130; `STAMP_FRESH_MS = 60*60_000`, hook.ts:149). Three M7 rules follow: no batch may add a write on the session-start path (the bar names that NOT SIMPLE, and MC-10's `hook [on|off]` writes only `~/.claude/settings.json`); EVERY sync takes the per-team mutex, not just the hook (sync.ts:102-104's D-R4 ruling, so `team leave` cannot be raced); and the app must never sync on a timer, because its own sync writes the stamp and suppresses the real hook for an hour.
